events.description: Bin Ladin returned to Afghanistan and began forging close ties to Pakistani militant groups.
Taliban came to power in Afghanistan and took control of militant training camps, increasing access for Pakistani militants.
After 11 September, Islamabad took steps to bolster domestic stability and limit the influence of radical militant groups.
Usama Bin Ladin returned to Afghanistan.
The Taliban came to power in Afghanistan and took control of militant training camps there.
After 11 September, Islamabad took steps to bolster domestic stability and limit radical militant groups' influence.
CIA assessment of extremists threatening US diplomatic, commercial and civilian interests in Pakistan, encouraged by Bin Ladin.

key_claims: Bin Ladin is strongly encouraging attacks on US diplomatic, civilian and commercial interests in Pakistan.
Since 1996 Bin Ladin has forged close ties to Pakistani militant groups, particularly those connected to the Taliban.
The Taliban takeover in 1996 gave Pakistani militants increased access to training camps in Afghanistan.
Pakistani militants share ideology and the Kashmir cause with Bin Ladin and the Taliban.
Arab extremists based in Afghanistan may also threaten attacks in Pakistan.
